clue.text: Dan, a shy Swede, resolved to repent then

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken up and reworked, so the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Swedish man called Dan, normally bashful, makes up his mind to say sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' signals the anagram of DAN A SHY SWEDE. 'to' is a link; 'repent then' points to the day itself, the start of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of Lent is a Christian day of penitence, marked with ashes on the forehead.

clue.text: Sign to get a universal food-enhancer

parts.note: U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
a spice is something added to improve the flavour of food

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: a seasoning that improves anything you cook is a good omen.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is an omen or portent, a token of what is to come.

clue.text: Listen to why he joined a riotous assembly

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd or a riot

explanation.surface: Someone asks to hear the reason a man took part in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why' and 'joined' are linking words here; HE, A and ROUT simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear someone out is to listen to everything they have to say before replying.

clue.text: Hungry Exeter MP sadly appears on the spur of the moment

definitions.text: on the spur of the moment

indicators.note: sadly in the sense of badly or wretchedly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a hungry person has had nothing to eat, nothing being the round letter O

explanation.surface: A famished member of parliament for Exeter makes a sorry impromptu appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' signals the anagram of O (from 'Hungry', empty) plus EXETER and MP; 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extempore describes speech or action done without preparation, improvised.

clue.text: Us space agency procures large rhino

parts.note: NASA is the United States space agency
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: NASA acquires a big rhinoceros for some reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhino' is not the animal but the Greek root meaning nose, as in rhinoplasty; 'procures' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek combining form rhino- means relating to the nose, which is what nasal also means.

clue.text: Little effusion from diocesan attendant

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese, so diocesan points to it
a page is a boy attendant, at a wedding or at court

explanation.surface: A small outpouring from a bishop's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is a slow leaking of liquid, a small flowing out.

clue.text: Question an engineer quizzically

parts.note: to question is to ask
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: Quiz an engineer with a puzzled look.
explanation.definitionFit: To look askance is to look with doubt or suspicion, a sideways questioning glance.

clue.text: Auction one's goods to stand for part of greater Manchester

parts.note: to stand as a candidate is to put up
Sale is a town in Trafford, Greater Manchester

explanation.surface: A Mancunian plans to sell up and run for office in his part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town south-west of Manchester city centre; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things up for sale is to offer them to buyers, as at an auction.

clue.text: Promotes bitter social-climber

parts.note: to up someone is to raise or promote them
tart means sharp or sour in taste

explanation.surface: A bitter person keeps advancing himself, a classic social climber.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly in status and behaves arrogantly, a parvenu.

clue.text: Make one's voice heard

parts.note: a plain description of talking louder or stating one's view openly

explanation.definitionFit: To speak louder, or to say what one thinks without holding back.

clue.text: Maybe gained through hazardous activity

parts.note: per is Latin for through or by means of
an adventure is a risky or daring undertaking

explanation.surface: Something possibly won by taking a dangerous gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gained' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Peradventure is an archaic word for perhaps or by chance.

clue.text: University class lacking variety

parts.note: a form is a school class or year group

explanation.surface: A university course where everyone is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means unchanging, the same throughout.

clue.text: Student of English composer in Leicester's outskirts

indicators.note: in places the English composer inside the outskirts of Leicester
outskirts of the city name means its first and last letters only

parts.note: Thomas Arne was an English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A music student from England studying a composer on the edge of Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts' takes the first and last letters of Leicester, L and R; 'in' puts E plus ARNE between them. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying or being taught.

clue.text: Quick to emerge from old London prison

definitions.meaning: a notorious London prison, mainly for debtors, until 1842

explanation.surface: Someone escapes swiftly from a historic London jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to emerge from' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift of foot, and also the name of a debtors' jail beside the Fleet river in London.

clue.text: Unceasingly admit others are improving

indicators.note: admit means let in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: on end means continuously, as in for hours on end
them means other people, as in us and them

explanation.surface: Someone keeps confessing that other people are getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admit' puts THEM inside ON END; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the mend means recovering, getting better after illness or trouble.

clue.text: Sam's Latin translation charms

indicators.note: a translation changes the form of the words, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sam produces a Latin version of some lucky charms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' signals the anagram of SAMS and LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object believed to bring luck or protection, an amulet.

clue.text: Made ballinger conjure up memories

indicators.note: made in the sense of formed or fashioned anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Ballinger caused people to reminisce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' signals the anagram of BALLINGER, which looks like a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rings a bell when it sounds familiar and stirs a recollection.

clue.text: The profit trawlermen hope for

parts.note: fishermen hope their trawl will bring in plenty, read as profit after costs

explanation.definitionFit: Net gain is profit left after deductions; fishermen want a full net.

clue.text: A Spanish aunt supports people with severe retardation

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits below the other

parts.note: men means people in general
tia is the Spanish word for aunt

explanation.surface: A Spanish aunt helps people with serious learning difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts TIA below A MEN in the down light; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amentia is a dated medical term for severe mental deficiency from birth.

clue.text: Model embraces swollen-headed lawmen

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to model is to pose

indicators.note: headed means only the head, the first letter of swollen, is used

explanation.surface: A fashion model hugs some arrogant sheriffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swollen-headed' reads as conceited, but '-headed' gives the first letter of 'swollen', S, which 'embraces' puts inside POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group of men summoned by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Groom means to shave in advance

parts.note: pre is the prefix meaning before or in advance
to pare is to trim or shave off thinly

explanation.surface: A bridegroom intends to shave before the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is the verb, to get ready, not the bridegroom. 'means to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom someone is to get them ready for a role.

clue.text: Ready to include us agents in the section

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
G-men are US federal agents of the FBI

explanation.surface: Prepared to take FBI agents into the department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts GMEN inside SET; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or portion cut off from a whole.

clue.text: Cockney sounds cruel, but is actually naïve

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H, so the word is heard without it

parts.note: heartless means cruel, without pity

explanation.surface: A Londoner seems unkind but is in fact innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop the H at the start of words. 'but is actually' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or cunning, simple and innocent.

clue.text: Eminent Muslim takes express to Idaho

parts.note: to express is to say
ID is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Idaho

explanation.surface: An important Muslim catches an express train to Idaho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like a train but is the verb. 'takes' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A sayid or sayyid is an honorific for a Muslim descended from Muhammad.

clue.text: The Italian's invisible dexterity?

indicators.note: in places the Italian article inside the word for what is visible

parts.note: something visible is in sight, giving sight
le is an Italian word for the, used before feminine plurals

explanation.surface: An Italian man's skill is so deft it cannot be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invisible' splits as 'in visible': LE (the Italian's) is in SIGHT. 'The Italian's' reads 'The Italian is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means deftness of hand, as in a conjuror's sleight of hand.

clue.text: Accurately produced? Quite so!

explanation.surface: Something was made with precision, and someone wholeheartedly agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means precisely and also serves as an exclamation agreeing with a speaker.

clue.text: Dilettante partner in a biblical city

indicators.note: in places the partner inside the letters for a and the city

parts.note: Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's city in the Bible
a mate is a partner or companion

explanation.surface: A dabbling companion living in an ancient city of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art without professional skill; an amateur likewise is a non-professional.

clue.text: Prior to decline, Peruvian was glowing

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the Peruvian goes in front of the decline

parts.note: Incan describes the native people of ancient Peru
a descent is a downward slope or decline

explanation.surface: Before a fall, a Peruvian was shining with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior to' puts INCAN before DESCENT; 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means emitting light because of great heat, shining brightly.
